standard.title: Literary devices shape meaning
standard.description: discuss the effects of some literary devices used to enhance meaning and shape the reader's imagination and emotions
standard.prior_knowledge: Students identify, reproduce and experiment with rhythmic sound and word patterns (AC9E2LE04). They have not yet discussed the effects of named literary devices — particularly imagery and sound devices like onomatopoeia — on meaning and the reader's experience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students discuss the effects of literary devices including imagery, sound devices and figurative language that enhance meaning and shape imagination and emotions.

nodes.label: Imagery and its effects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify imagery (visual, nature, sensory) in a text and discuss the effect it creates for the reader's imagination.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one piece of imagery in a text and discuss what picture or sensation it creates for the reader.
nodes.typical_width: Discuss the effects of imagery in texts — including imagery related to nature, senses and familiar experiences — explaining what the imagery makes readers see, feel or imagine.
wider: Compare imagery used to describe the same natural phenomenon (e.g. a storm, a river) in two different texts and discuss how different choices create different effects
Explore how imagery in a First Nations Australian text conveys a relationship with Country/Place that goes beyond description
success_criteria: Student identifies imagery in a text (naming what is being described)
Student discusses the effect on the reader — what the imagery makes them imagine, see or feel

nodes.label: Sound devices and questions about effects
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify sound devices such as onomatopoeia, alliteration and rhyme in texts and discuss why the poet or author chose them.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least one sound device in a text and discuss one effect it creates — answering the question of why the author might have used it.
nodes.typical_width: Generate questions to discuss the effects of literary devices; identify onomatopoeia, alliteration, rhyme and other sound devices and discuss how they enhance meaning, add rhythm or create sound effects that shape the reader's imagination.
wider: Experiment with replacing sound device words with neutral synonyms and compare the effect — discussing what is lost
Explore how onomatopoeia works across different languages and cultures — discussing whether sound imitation is universal or language-specific

response_modes.reason: Students can identify sound devices but struggle to discuss their effects beyond 'it sounds good'. Experiencing devices across poetry, narrative and non-fiction contexts — and generating questions about why authors chose them — builds analytical habit rather than just identification.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The questioning approach ('why does the poet use onomatopoeia here?') is a rich pedagogical entry point for Y3. It shifts from identification to genuine literary discussion and builds habits of literary inquiry that are intrinsically engaging at this year level.
success_criteria: Student identifies a sound device and names its type (onomatopoeia, alliteration, rhyme)
Student discusses an effect the device creates — not just that it 'sounds good'
